{{Short description|Disjunction in formal semantics}}
In [[formal semantics (natural language)|formal semantics]], a '''Hurford disjunction''' is a [[disjunction]] in which one of the disjuncts [[entailment|entails]] the other. The concept was first identified by British linguist [[James Hurford]].<ref>{{cite journal| title=Exclusive or Inclusive Disjunction| last1=Hurford| first1=James R.| journal=Foundations of Language| year=1974| volume=11| issue=3| pages=409–411| jstor=25000785}}</ref> The sentence "Mary is in the Netherlands or she is in Amsterdam" is an example of a Hurford disjunction since one cannot be in Amsterdam without being in the Netherlands. Other examples are shown below:<ref name = "cambridgehbk" >{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Schlenker |first1=Philippe |editor-last1=Aloni |editor-first1=Maria|editor1-link=Maria Aloni |editor-last2=Dekker |editor-first2=Paul |encyclopedia=Cambridge Handbook of Formal Semantics |title=The Semantics-Pragmatics Interface |year=2016 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-02839-5 |doi=10.1017/CBO9781139236157.023|pages=685–687}}</ref><ref name = "inqsembook" >{{cite book |last1=Ciardelli |first1=Ivano |last2=Groenendijk |first2=Jeroen |last3=Roelofsen |first3=Floris |year=2018 |title= Inquisitive semantics |doi=10.1093/oso/9780198814788.001.0001 |publisher= Oxford University Press |pages=183–186 |isbn=9780198814788|url=http://library.oapen.org/bitstream/20.500.12657/25127/1/Inquisitive_Semantics_9780192546388_WEB.PDF }}</ref>

# #Tamina saw a Beatle or Paul McCartney.
# #The number I'm thinking of is divisible by 4 or it's even.
# #Is Wilbur a pig or an animal?

As indicated by the [[octothorp]]s in the above examples, Hurford disjunctions are typically [[felicity (pragmatics)|infelicitous]]. Their infelicity has been argued to arise from them being redundant, since simply uttering the stronger of the two disjuncts would have had the same semantic effect. Thus, they have been taken as motivation for a principle such as the following:<ref name = "inqsembook" /><ref>{{cite conference |title= Hurford disjunctions: embedded exhaustification and structural economy |last1=Katzir |first1=Roni |last2=Singh|first2=Raj|year= 2013|conference=Sinn und Bedeutung |volume=18|url=https://ojs.ub.uni-konstanz.de/sub/index.php/sub/article/view/313}}</ref>

:'''Local Redundancy''': An utterance is infelicitous if its logical form contains an instance of a binary operator <math>\oplus </math> applied to arguments <math>A</math> or <math>B</math>, whose semantic contribution is contextually equivalent to that of either <math>A</math> or <math>B</math> on its own.

However, some particular instances of Hurford disjunctions are felicitous.<ref name = "cambridgehbk" /><ref name=Chierchia2009>{{cite encyclopedia |last1=Chierchia |first1=Gennaro |last2=Fox |first2=Danny| last3=Spector |first3=Benjamin |editor-last1= Egré |editor-first1=Paul | editor-last2= Magri |editor-first2=Giorgio |encyclopedia=Presuppositions and implicature |title= Hurford's constraint and the theory of scalar implicatures: evidence for embedded implicaturess|year= 2009|publisher=MIT Press}}</ref>

# Sofia ate some of the pizza or all of it.
# Henrietta is five feet tall or six feet tall.

Felicitous Hurford disjunctions have been analyzed by positing that the weaker disjunct is strengthened by an [[subordination (linguistics)|embedded]] [[scalar implicature]] which eliminates the entailment between the disjuncts. For instance, in the first of the felicitous examples above, the left disjunct's unenriched meaning is simply that Sofia ate a nonzero amount of pizza. This would result in a redundancy violation since eating all the pizza entails eating a nonzero amount of it. However, if an embedded scalar implicature enriches this disjunct so that it denotes the proposition that that Sofia ate some ''but not all'' of the pizza, this entailment no longer goes through. Eating all of the pizza does not entail eating some but not all of it. Thus, Local Redundancy will still be satisfied.<ref name = "cambridgehbk" /><ref name=Chierchia2009/>
